condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I. A.1. The Borrower shall, through the Ministry of Environment (“MoE”), not later than thirty (30) days afterthe Effective Date, or such later date as agreed with the Bank, establish and thereafter maintain at all times during theimplementation of the Project, a Project Steering Committee with a composition (comprising, inter alia, the ministries ofenvironment, planning and economic development, local development, transport, health and population, international cooperation, theCairo, Qalyubia and Giza governorates and the Cairo Transport Authority), mandate, terms of reference and resources satisfactory tothe Bank, to be responsible for, inter alia: (a) providing strategic and policy guidance on matters relating to the Project; and(b) coordinating inter-agency and inter-ministerial policies and roles, all in accordance with the provisions of the ProjectOperational Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I. A.2. (b) The Borrower shall, through MoE, not later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, or suchlater date as agreed with the Bank, establish and thereafter maintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, aProject Coordination Unit (“PCU”) with a composition, terms of reference and resources acceptable to the Bank. The PCU shall beresponsible for the overall coordination of the implementation and management (including technical procurement, financialmanagement, environmental and social aspects, monitoring, evaluation, reporting and communication) of Project activities andresults, all in accordance with the provisions of the Project Operational Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I. A.3. The Borrower shall, through each participating ministry, department or agency, not later than thirty(30) days after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed with the Bank, establish and thereafter maintain at all timesduring the implementation of the Project, a Technical Implementation Unit, with a composition, mandate, terms of reference andresources satisfactory to the Bank. Each Technical Implementation Unit shall be responsible for the day to day coordination,implementation and management of activities under its respective part of the Project, all in accordance with the provisions of theProject Operational Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I. B.1. (a) To facilitate the implementation of the Project, the Borrower shall, through the MoE, not laterthan thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed with the Bank, prepare and adopt a Project OperationalManual in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank (“POM”), and such POM shall include, inter alia, the descriptionof:(i) detailed institutional arrangements including roles and responsibilities of various agencies for Project implementation;(ii) procurement arrangements; (iii) applicable environmental and social arrangements including a grievance redressmechanism;(iv) detailed financial management and disbursement arrangements and audit procedures; and(v) reporting, monitoring andevaluation arrangements.

Schedule 2, Section I. B.2. (a) The Borrower shall, through MoE, not later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, enterinto an Inter-Ministerial Agreement with inter alia, the MoLD, MoHP, MoT, Cairo governorate, Cairo governorate and Qalyubiagovernorate, or any other participating ministry, department or agency, in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.

comment.narrative: The project funded a public awareness and communications campaign for the 2024 Black Cloud season including TV video clips. Over 391 face to face meetings and seminars with stakeholders and media were held across Greater Cairo Governates: Cairo (46); Eastern Province (40); Dakahlia G.; Gharbia (184); Al Beheria (55). title.narrative: Reduction of large-scale solid waste fires per annum

comment.narrative:
This primarily assesses the reduction of large-scale solid waste fires in the governorate of Qalyubia and Cairo based on project investments.
The project also supports the reduction of waste burning across 9 Governates of Greater Cairo during the Black Cloud season.
In the 2024 season the government reported 210 interventions to combat incidents of open waste burning across 6 Delta Governates. Systems deployed used satellite monitoring, complaints from citizens, and enforcement teams on the ground.
A new Black Cloud Graded Response Action Plan is in an advanced stage of preparation for 2025 which will further systematize monitoring during the peak air pollution season.

title.narrative: Black Carbon emissions from public buses
Black Carbon emissions from public buses

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the change in GHG emissions due to the introduction of e-buses, compared to the business as usual using ICE buses. The project expects to reduce the GHG emissions. The baseline is normalized to equal 100% and the target shows the expected reduction against this base.
A consultant study was completed in October, 2024 to establish baseline information and methodologies. The CDM Method for estimating PM2.5 emissions were first applied and then the Climate and Clean Air Coalition methodology for estimating Black Carbon for the Logistics Sector was used. PM2.5 estimated for existing buses operating on 5 CTA routes resulting in 0.177 tons/year. A ratio of 0.74 was applied for a baseline BC estimate of 0.16 tons/yr. BC estimates for the e-bus fleet were estimated at 0.012 tons/yr for a reduction against baseline of 92.7. While still very high, the final target could be reduced accordingly.

title.narrative: Greenhouse gas emissions (CO2 equiv.) from public buses on selected routes

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the change in GHG emissions due to the introduction of e-buses, compared to the business as usual using internal combustion engines (ICE) buses. The project expects to reduce the GHG emissions. The baseline is normalized to equal 100% and the target shows the expected reduction against this base.
Status update: A consultant study was completed in October, 2024 to establish baseline information and methodologies. The COPERT methodology was used for existing buses operating on 5 CTA routes resulting in 4438.09 tons CO2-eq. Estimates for the E-bus fleet were made using the CDM Tool07 at 2944.23 tons CO2/yr. This indicated the project may be able to over-achieve the target to attain 66%.

title.narrative: Institutional Air Quality response mechanism established and operational

comment.narrative:
A national system is established and operational, that allows the Government to take decisions during high pollution days based on air quality forecasting.
Status: An updated Draft Institutional Response Mechanism has been prepared. Consultants mobilized worked with the Ministry and stakeholders on a proposed Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) for Greater Cairo to be introduced for the 2025 Black Cloud Season. A workshop on the draft GRAP was held during the World Bank mission. The GRAP is pending final endorsement by the Ministry / EEAA and the Inter-Government Committee for the Response for the Black Cloud.

title.narrative: Greater Cairo Climate and Air Quality Management Plan developed and submitted to the Council of Ministers

comment.narrative:
An Integrated Climate and Air Quality Management Plan (IC-AQMP) will be developed to serve as the overarching framework for government action to reduce the sources and amounts of pollutants responsible for the degradation of urban ambient air quality and regional and global warming. Plan will present options with estimated budget requirements in the form of a time-bound action plan with clear roles and responsibilities delineated.
Status: The launch event was held on June 6, 2023 and the procurement for a consultancy is underway.

title.narrative: Greater Cairo Climate and Air Quality Management Plan developed and submitted to the Council of Ministers

comment.narrative:
An Integrated Climate and Air Quality Management Plan (IC-AQMP) will be developed to serve as the overarching framework for government multi-sector action to reduce the sources and amounts of pollutants responsible for the degradation of urban ambient air quality and regional and global warming. The plan will present options with estimated budget requirements in the form of a time-bound action plan with clear roles and responsibilities delineated.
Status: A consultant firm was hired in summer 2024 to support the preparation process including AQM modeling to underpin the plan. Work on the Black Cloud Action Plan proceeded in parallel and will also inform the IC-AQMP. Stakeholder discussions on the long-term IC-AQMP with key ministries have been held. A multi-sector stakeholder workshop is planned for May 2025.

title.narrative: Percentage ofâ€¯grievances received and addressed in a timely manner

comment.narrative:
This indicator refers to the percentage of grievances that are addressed and responded to within a timeline that has been specified and publicly communicated by the project. It also assesses the functionality of the GRM system against the following specific parameters: (i) Standard operational guidelines for the system are developed; (ii) Qualified staff has been appointed to deal with the complaints; and (iii) Reporting system is in place to document and track complaints.
Status: The project has a GRM system. Civil works contractors hired under the project are also required to have active GRM systems. The 10th of Ramadan contractor has a GRM system in place that has been used to identify and resolve issues (% addressed in a timely manner TBC). Success of the government's enforcement in the Black Cloud in 2024 is partly attributed to over 80 reports and complaints from citizens about illegal burning of agricultural waste, municipal waste, and industrial waste.

comment.narrative:

This would involve selection of eligible contractor/ operator, signing of contract signed with a private operator, and regular receipt of waste at the facility.
Status: The 10th of Ramadan Integrated Solid Waste Management Facility (ISWMF) basic infrastructure and two associated waste transfer facilities are under construction. A financial model for a Design-Build-Finance-Operate long-term municipal waste contract has been completed with inputs from private sector consultations. A PPP transaction advisory consulting a firm has been selected to work with the Ministry of Finance PPP Unit on the tender structure starting in April 2025.
